steps.name: Count matrix QC, filtering, and PCA
caveats: Counts may be raw or length-corrected (countsFromAbundance setting unknown); do not attempt to infer gene lengths — DESeq2 does not use them for this contrast.
Metadata has only 2 columns, so no covariates other than condition exist; do not invent a batch term for the single-batch design.
Do not compute TPM-like normalization for the DE steps; size-factor normalization is handled by DESeq2 downstream.
steps.context: Data: /eval-four-models-v2-without-salmon-counts-unknown-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 13 cols) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-salmon-counts-unknown-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows x 2 cols, presumably sample id + condition). Design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, one batch. The Salmon quant.sf files are absent and countsFromAbundance is unknown.
steps.question: Are the delivered counts.csv and metadata.csv internally consistent (sample alignment, integer-valued counts, two clean condition labels of 6 vs 6), which genes pass low-count filtering, and do treated and control samples separate in unsupervised PCA without outliers?
steps.description: Load the delivered gene-level count CSV and the 12x2 metadata CSV, verify that sample identifiers match 1:1 and that the condition column contains exactly two labels (treated vs control as written in the file), and test count-matrix integrity: non-negativity, integer vs non-integer values (which discriminates raw counts from length-corrected Salmon output and must be reported either way), duplicated gene identifiers, and the fraction of zero rows. Apply a standard low-count filter (keep genes with a count of 10 or more in a reasonable minimum number of samples, e.g. CPM > 1 in at least the smaller group size) and report how many genes survive. Run an unsupervised PCA on log-transformed filtered counts (log2(counts+1) or a simple variance-stabilizing transform) to visualize treated-vs-control separation, flag any sample that clusters with the wrong group or sits as an extreme outlier on PC1/PC2, and save the filtered matrix plus the QC report for the DE step. This step needs no reference data.
acceptance_criteria: counts.csv and metadata.csv row/sample identifiers are matched 1:1 with explicit handling of any mismatch (report, never silently drop)
integer-vs-float check on the count table is recorded, together with its implication for the unknown Salmon/tximport provenance
low-count filtering applied with the gene-retention count reported per condition
PCA on log-transformed data saved with the first two PCs and treatment/control labels; outliers flagged by name if present

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression treated vs control
caveats: With 6 vs 6 the analysis is adequately powered for strong signals but small effects will be missed; do not over-interpret marginal FDR values.
If the count table turns out to be non-integer (length-corrected), DESeq2 will round internally — report this fact in the output rather than switching methods.
Do not include a batch term; the design statement says one batch, and the metadata carries no batch column.
steps.context: Input: the filtered count matrix and QC report from T1S1. 12 samples, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, no batch covariate. The Salmon countsFromAbundance setting is unknown; DESeq2's size-factor model does not require gene lengths for this contrast, so proceed on the delivered matrix regardless of provenance and note the provenance caveat in the output.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control (6 vs 6, unpaired) at FDR < 0.05, and what are their effect sizes?
steps.description: Run differential expression on the filtered matrix from T1S1 with DESeq2 using design ~ condition, contrasting treated vs control with the control group as reference level. Estimate size factors, dispersions, and Wald statistics; apply independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Compute apeglm-shrunk log2 fold changes (lfcShrink, type apeglm) for ranking and reporting, keeping both raw and shrunk estimates in the output table. Save the full ranked results table (all tested genes: baseMean, log2FC, shrunk log2FC, stat, p-value, padj), the significant gene list at FDR < 0.05, and a summary of counts by direction. Flag any gene whose identifier mapping is ambiguous. This step needs no reference data.
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 model run with ~ condition and a Wald test; model formula and reference level recorded
Full results table saved (gene, baseMean, log2FC, shrink-adjusted log2FC, SE, stat, p-value, padj) plus a gene symbol/identifier column carried from counts.csv
Number of significant genes reported at FDR < 0.05 (and optionally log2FC >= 1), split by direction, with the count of rows lost to independent filtering
Named top up- and down-regulated genes listed in the output for interpretability

steps.name: DE results visualization
caveats: Label figure values with shrunk LFCs to avoid over-emphasizing low-count high-LFC genes.
Keep gene labels readable (ggrepel or EnhancedVolcano labeling); do not crowd plots with 100+ labels.
steps.context: Input: the DESeq2 results table and the variance-stabilized matrix from T1S2/T1S1. Condition labels are treated vs control as written in metadata.csv.
steps.question: What do the treated-vs-control differential expression results look like as a volcano plot, a top-gene heatmap, and a labeled PCA?
steps.description: Produce publication-quality summary figures from the T1S2 results: (1) a volcano plot of shrunk log2FC vs -log10(FDR) with the most significant genes labeled, (2) a heatmap of the top differentially expressed genes (e.g. top 30 by shrunk log2FC among significant genes, plus strongest down-regulated) on variance-stabilized counts with the condition annotation bar, and (3) a labeled PCA plot re-using the T1S1 transform with treated/control coloring. Save all figures plus a CSV of the top-N DE genes for reporting. This step needs no reference data.
acceptance_criteria: Volcano plot (shrunk log2FC vs -log10 padj) with labeled leading genes saved
Heatmap of top DE genes (by shrunk LFC among significant ones) with condition labels, saved
PCA figure from T1S1 re-emitted or referenced with condition labels for the final report
All figures written as files with sensible names; no figure depends on un-run code

steps.name: WikiPathways enrichment of DE results
caveats: The WikiPathways collection is smaller than MSigDB hallmark/GO; treat it as an interpretive overlay, not an exhaustive map.
If the top DE genes are mostly unannotated or the ranked list has a weak signal, GSEA may return few significant pathways — report that honestly.
Gene identifier space: counts.csv identifiers must be matched to HGNC symbols; report any identifier-space mismatch rate rather than silently dropping genes.
steps.context: Input: the full ranked DE results table (statistic or shrunk log2FC) from T1S2 for ~10-12k genes. Reference data available in this environment: a WikiPathways Homo sapiens GMT under /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/ with HGNC gene-symbol members ('%'-delimited descriptor per line). Use it if present; the environment may also hold other human gene-set collections that the executing agent can check for, but no network access exists — only provisioned references are usable.
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes up- or down-regulated in treated vs control skin, and which genes drive them?
steps.description: Run gene-set enrichment on the treated-vs-control result to place the DE genes in biological context. Use fgsea on the full ranked gene list (ranked by the Wald statistic or shrunk log2FC) against a WikiPathways human pathway gene-set collection (GMT with HGNC symbols, provisioned in the environment), matching gene identifiers from counts.csv to HGNC symbols. In parallel, run over-representation analysis on the significant-gene list at FDR < 0.05. Report per-pathway NES, FDR, and leading-edge genes, and check whether AD-relevant pathways (skin barrier, immune signaling, Th2 cytokine axis) appear. If the WikiPathways human GMT is absent from the environment at run time, report the gap explicitly and emit the ranked list so enrichment can be rerun once sets are provisioned.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the full ranked DEStat vector (not just significant genes), minSize >= 10, multiple-testing-adjusted pathway FDRs reported
Leading-edge genes per enriched pathway captured in the output table
Direction of pathway-level signal (up in treated vs down in treated) distinguishable from the ranking statistic sign
If the GMT is absent, the step reports that no enrichment result was produced rather than substituting an unverified set

plan.title: AD treated-vs-control DESeq2 DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is one Salmon-derived gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples) plus a 12-row metadata table labeling 6 treated vs 6 control human skin samples (atopic dermatitis lesional vs control), unpaired and single-batch. Because the per-sample quant.sf files were not delivered, the provenance of the counts (raw counts vs length-corrected countsFromAbundance output) is unknown. DESeq2's model uses size factors rather than gene lengths, so its treatment-vs-control inference is valid for either provenance; the plan therefore does not attempt to reconstruct tximport settings, but the first step verifies count integrity (integer vs non-integer values) so the report can state which scenario held. The pipeline is the standard one for a small two-group bulk RNA-seq contrast: QC/filtering with an unsupervised PCA to catch outliers and verify condition separation, a DESeq2 Wald-test differential expression analysis with log2FC shrinkage, results visualization, and pathway-level interpretation using the provisioned WikiPathways human gene sets. All steps run on the delivered CSVs; no downloads are planned.
